name: Materials for Cryogenic Service
summary: Covers how materials behave near absolute zero and which ones are used for liquid-hydrogen and liquid-oxygen tanks, superconducting magnets and cryogenic instruments.

topics.name: Cryogenic environments: LN2, LOX, LH2 and liquid helium
Temperature dependence of strength, toughness and ductility; the ductile-brittle transition
FCC metals at low temperature: austenitic stainless steels, aluminium and copper alloys
Aluminium-lithium alloys for cryogenic propellant tanks
Thermal contraction and thermal conductivity at low temperature
Polymers and composites at cryogenic temperatures: embrittlement and microcracking
Hydrogen embrittlement and permeation in LH2 systems
Oxygen compatibility and ignition hazards in LOX systems
Superconducting materials for magnets: Nb-Ti, Nb3Sn, MgB2 and REBCO tapes
